title: Separable extensions are filtered colimits of smooth algebras
statement:
Let $L/K$ be a separable extension of fields. Then $L$ is a filtered
colimit of finitely generated smooth $K$-algebras, and the colimit may be
taken over smooth $K$-subalgebras of $L$ with the inclusions as transition
maps; consequently $\Spec(L)$ is the inverse limit of the corresponding
affine smooth $K$-schemes with affine transition morphisms.
(*Source:* Stacks Project, Algebra, Lemma 10.158.11,
[Tag `07BV`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07BV); the
finitely generated case is the imported statement
[lem-kun-fg-separable-smooth] and the algebraic case is proved in this
chapter.)

proof.text: For a finite subset s of L, construct F = IntermediateField.adjoin K s. This field is finitely generated (IntermediateField.fg_adjoin_finset), equivalently essentially of finite type (IntermediateField.essFiniteType_iff). The hypothesis hsep makes F/K separably generated, so [lem-weil-pbc-separably-generated-separable] makes it separable. Apply [lem-kun-fg-separable-smooth] to F/K to obtain a nonempty directed family of finitely generated smooth subalgebras covering F.

Induction on a finite set in a directed covering family puts all its elements in a single member: choose any index for the empty set, and a common upper bound for the induction member and a member containing the inserted element. Apply this inside F to the lifts of s. Map the resulting subalgebra along F.val into L; Subalgebra.equivMapOfInjective transfers smoothness by Algebra.Smooth.of_equiv, and Subalgebra.FG.map transfers finite generation. Thus every finite subset of L lies in a finitely generated smooth subalgebra.

Apply finite-subset coverage to the empty set to get nonemptiness, to the union of finite generating sets of two smooth finitely generated subalgebras to get a common upper bound (Algebra.adjoin_le), and to singleton sets to get elementwise coverage.

Give the smooth-subalgebra index its directed-order instance. The underlying cocone of types is a colimit by Types.FilteredColimit.isColimitOf': coverage gives surjectivity, and each inclusion is injective by Subtype.ext, so equal elements are already equal at their own index. The forgetful functor from CommRingCat preserves filtered colimits and reflects isomorphisms; reflect the colimit with isColimitOfReflects. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-spec-colimit-limit], using isLimitOfPreserves Scheme.Spec hc.op and the affine-source/affine-target instance. Smoothness of each algebra is its index predicate.

lean.statement: theorem separable_extension_is_filtered_colimit_smooth {K : Type u} {L : Type v} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L] (hsep : Algebra.IsSeparableExtension K L) : Nonempty {A : Subalgebra K L // Algebra.Smooth K A ∧ A.FG} ∧ Directed (· ≤ ·) (fun A : {A : Subalgebra K L // Algebra.Smooth K A ∧ A.FG} => A.1) ∧ (∀ x : L, ∃ A : {A : Subalgebra K L // Algebra.Smooth K A ∧ A.FG}, x ∈ A.1) ∧ Nonempty (IsColimit (smoothSubalgebraCocone K L)) ∧ Nonempty (IsLimit (Scheme.Spec.mapCone (smoothSubalgebraCocone K L).op)) ∧ (∀ A : {A : Subalgebra K L // Algebra.Smooth K A ∧ A.FG}, Algebra.Smooth K A.1) ∧ (∀ (A B : {A : Subalgebra K L // Algebra.Smooth K A ∧ A.FG}) (f : B ⟶ A), IsAffineHom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Subalgebra.inclusion (leOfHom f)).toRingHom)))
